newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets import plan to cover diesel shortage.
newsitem.headline: China sets import plan to cover diesel shortage.

text.p: China, struggling to cope with an unexpected diesel supply crisis, has set plans to ensure sufficient imports to cover a hefty shortfall, the China Daily said on Sunday.
The newspaper's Business Weekly said the shipment of two million tonnes was expected to arrive this month and that more would be ordered to cover the gap.
It was not clear if the current import plan included shipments started in December, when officials first began to address the crisis.
The newspaper said China's diesel supplies ran dangerously low last year when regional oil companies ordered only 4.6 million tonnes instead of the 7.2 million called for under the government's plan.
That has aggravated an annual gap between domestic output and demand of five to six million tonnes.
"Permanent state reserves for emergencies are becoming urgent because of the nationwide diesel supply crisis," the newspaper said.

It said the crisis was sparked when regional oil companies stopped ordering diesel on international markets because prices were higher than those set domestically by China's inflation-wary bureaucrats.

Despite the state's price guidelines, the shortage sent China's diesel prices soaring to 4,000 yuan ($482) a tonne late last year from 2,270 yuan in August. Prices later stabilised at around 2,900 yuan after refineries stepped up production.
The newspaper said the diesel crisis had exposed China's "lack of a flexible, timely reaction mechanism for the pricing system to international market fluctuation."

To rectify the situation, the central government has established an import plan and authorised state-run Sinopec as the only company empowered to buy on international markets, cutting regional oil companies out of the fuel oil import business, the newspaper said.
The newspaper said the government would maintain its controlled pricing system for crude and fuel oils, which Beijing sees as a bulwark against inflation.

The government permitted the basic price of diesel to rise 90 yuan per tonne in October, and another 200 yuan in December to bring the price to 2,190 yuan per tonne, "close to the expected or market-required level", the newspaper said.
The basic price of crude oil rose 85 yuan per tonne, but is still 350 yuan lower than the international level, it said.
China's diesel production rose 11 percent in 1996 to 43.25 million tonnes.
China produced 3.845 million tonnes of diesel in January this year, up 12 percent year on year, the State Statistical Bureau said.
